title: Adaptive Batch Sizing Wizard and Quant Snapshot Exporter
author: Maya Singh
description: Summary: Introduces an interactive 'Batch Sizing Wizard' service and a companion 'quant-snapshot-exporter'. The wizard computes tenant-aware default batching and cache presets by combining lightweight workload sampling with a rule-based fallback and a dry-run unit-econ simulator. The exporter creates versioned quantization profile snapshots (per-model, per-hardware-class) to decouple runtime selection from ongoing autotuning experiments. Motivation: customers frequently hit suboptimal defaults when moving from dev to dedicated/private deployments; manually tuning batching/caching/quantization is time-consuming and often risk-averse. This change bundle aims to automate safe defaults while providing transparent dry-run economics and a rollback path. Key capabilities: 1) Batch Sizing Wizard: sampling daemon that runs short microbursts against a shadow runtime, reports latency/cost curvature, suggests three candidate templates (latency-first, balanced, cost-first) and a suggested default. Templates include batch_size, max_wait_ms, kv_cache_ttl, and prefill_window. Built-in safety: canary rollout, per-tenant warmstart, automatic rollback if tail-latency or token-cost regressions exceed thresholds. 2) Quant Snapshot Exporter: periodically captures quantization metrics (int8/4-bit profile success rates, dequantization overhead, per-sequence slowdown) and exports signed JSON snapshots to model-registry-compatible storage. Snapshots annotated with hw-class tags (A100-80GB, L4, H100-80GB) and workload signatures so serving routing can pick a snapshot without running a fresh autotune. 3) Unit Econ Dry-Run: offline simulator that replays sampled traces against templates and quant snapshots to estimate 90/95/99 token p99 costs and expected SLO risk. Includes a CLI (redwood cost-wizard estimate --tenant X --template balanced --snapshot v2025-11-20). 4) Operator UX: Console flow that shows three suggested templates, delta against current defaults, expected monthly spend delta, and an action button to apply with a canary percent and auto-fallback policy. Implementation notes: sampling agent is implemented as a small Go daemon with pluggable probes; the wizard service runs as a k8s deployment behind the redwood-controlplane and writes suggestions to the policy-service API. Quant exporter is implemented as a background worker in the model-registry service (Python), with snapshots stored in S3 + signed metadata in Postgres. The dry-run simulator lives in the econ-sim package and is deterministic for repeatability. Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'batch_wizard_v1' feature flag; enabled initially for internal tenants and a small cohort of beta customers. Observability: new telemetry keys (wizard.sampling.latency_curve, wizard.suggestion.delta_cost_usd, quant.snap.success_rate) and dashboard panels added. Backwards compatibility: no runtime code path changes to serving; serving reads snapshots only when explicitly enabled by the control plane. Checklist: - [x] Sampling daemon + lightweight shadow runner - [x] Wizard service + API + Console integration - [x] Quant snapshot exporter + versioned storage - [x] Dry-run unit econ simulator + CLI - [x] Canary rollout + automatic rollback policies - [x] Telemetry + dashboards - [x] Tests: unit + integration + a small canary in perf-lab Limitations: initial sampling focuses on small sequence length distributions and may underrepresent rare long-context workloads; fallback heuristics include forcing conservative defaults for tenants flagged as 'long-tail'. Related: builds on previous telemetry and batch-prefill work but intentionally avoids changing internal batching primitives to make the change low-risk. Linear references: ENG-3421 (wizard), ENG-3490 (quant snapshots).

release_notes: Adds an interactive Batch Sizing Wizard (tenant-aware default templates), a quant snapshot exporter for versioned quant profiles, and an offline unit-econ dry-run simulator. Feature is behind feature flag batch_wizard_v1 and will be rolled out via canary. See docs/ops/batch-wizard.md for operator guidance.
